text:
omar: noticed a tight P99 window this morning. a cluster of GPUs pulled the same 2 large shards concurrently and IO spiked.

anna: thanks for flagging. were those marked with any hot hints in the manifest?

omar: no hints, default manifest. prefetchers didn't batch them because they were split across groups.

lee: seems like a budgeting problem. if manifest had `hot_hint: {prob: 0.6, group: "g_net"}` prefetcher could prioritize and stagger pulls.

sara: agree. I'd add two fields: `hot_hint.probability` and `hot_hint.estimated_prefetch_bytes`. cheap and backward compatible.

omar: also propose a backpressure signal from loader: "prefetch_budget_exhausted" so router/runtime can delay admitting new requests for that model-version for a few ms instead of sending them all to GPUs.

lee: good call. that reduces thundering herd. loader already emits io_wait metrics; we can extend them to an admit-rejection event.

anna: minor naming nit: `hot_hint` vs `priority_hint`. prefer `priority_hint` to be clearer.

sara: +1 `priority_hint`. also we should have a global budget controller that limits concurrent shard pulls per-node to avoid overloading shared storage.

infra-bot: infra: starting a canary for per-node prefetch caps on cluster-gamma. token-based limiter enabled.

omar: follow-ups: (1) manifest PR adding priority_hint schema (omar), (2) loader: emit admit-rejections + budget metrics (lee), (3) router: honor prefetch backpressure and fallback to truncation/faster model (anna).

anna: short and actionable. will sync in next eng-ml sync. thank you everyone.
